newsitem.title: USA: RJR investors seen in new push for spinoff.
newsitem.headline: RJR investors seen in new push for spinoff.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Inc. could face a new round of shareholder pressure to break up its food and tobacco businesses after a spinoff announced Tuesday by American Brands Inc.

Investors Bennett LeBow and Carl Icahn, who earlier this year waged an unsuccessful proxy fight against RJR aimed at forcing a spinoff, were expected to use the American Brands action to drum up fresh support for their own cause.
LeBow reacted swiftly to the American Brands news, noting the financial attraction of a spinoff.

"Will RJR Nabisco follow the lead of American Brands and finally recognise that separating two completely unrelated businesses is the only way to unlock the substantial value of both entities?" LeBow said in a statement.

American Brands stock surged after it unveiled plans to spin off its British-based Gallaher tobacco unit from its other businesses, which include Jim Beam whisky, Master Lock padlocks and Cobra golf clubs.

Although LeBow and Icahn formally abandoned their effort after losing the proxy fight, both were expected to separately pursue a spinoff. Some industry experts and investors expect Icahn to launch a new proxy fight next year.

"Carl Icahn should use this to his greatest advantage," said Greg Jackson, portfolio manager at Yacktman Asset Management Co., which sold 1.4 million shares of RJR several months ago after being disappointed with its performance.
New York-based RJR has said it wants to spin off its 80.5 percent-owned Nabisco Holdings Corp., but insisted this was not the right time to break up the food and tobacco company.

Icahn, who raised his RJR stake to 5.8 percent in August, could not be reached for comment. LeBow is chairman of Brooke Group Ltd., which owns tobacco company Liggett Group Inc. He holds a 1.9 percent stake in RJR.
RJR has repeatedly said it wants to first improve the tobacco business and wait for a better tobacco litigation environment.
And any new investor agitation is unlikely to change that position.

"Our company remains committed to a spinoff, but at this point we still don't believe the timing is right. Our approach and strategy remain the same and the commitment remains the same," said RJR spokeswoman Carol Makovich, who described the the issues involving a potential RJR spinoff and the American Brands spinoff as "apples and oranges."
Unlike RJR, Old Greenwich, Conn.-based American Brands eliminated U.S. liability in 1994 when it sold its domestic tobacco business to Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T. Industries Plc.
RJR stock rose $1 to $27.625 on the New York Stock Exchange, in apparent sympathy with American Brands, which jumped $3.375 to $47.875, also on the NYSE.
"Some investors are extrapolating, rightly or wrongly," said analyst Emanuel Goldman at PaineWebber.
Nabisco products include Oreo cookies, Ritz crackers and grey Poupon mustard. The company's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco unit makes Winston and Camel and other brands.
"I don't think (the spinoff decision) is contagious,. I think the issues are different for the two companies," said Barbara Goodstein, a spinoff expert at Rothschild Inc.
American Brands said the spinoff would strengthen the company by removing it from the current harsh environment for cigarette makers in the United States.

With sales of over $6.5 billion for the 12 months through June, Gallaher, whose major brands include Benson and Hedges and Silk Cut, is the tobacco market leader in Britain, with strong international sales, principally in Europe.

Shares of Philip Morris Cos. Inc., the other giant U.S. food and tobacco company, showed little reaction, and were off 12.5 cents at $93.375 on the NYSE. The company, which has posted strong financial results and recently raised its dividend, has come under little pressure to split up its operations.
